chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I inform you of those who are most remote from me in likeness?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah!' He said: 'The immoral, the scandalous, the foul-mouthed, the stingy, the arrogant, the malicious, the envious, the hard of heart, the one remote from every hope of goodness, the one not safe from every evil feared.'

key_terms.الْحَقُودُ: The malicious or full of grudges
key_terms.الْمُتَفَحِّشُ: The one who exaggerates in vulgarity/scandal

ai.seo_question: What are the key character traits that make a person most remote from the Prophet in likeness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) links physical resemblance to spiritual proximity, identifying the 'Fahish' (one who is excessively indecent in speech and deed) as the one most distant from him. This classification highlights how external vulgarity reflects an internal hardness of heart (*Qasi al-Qalb*), a key concept in Shia ethics regarding the alignment of character with divine proximity. The description serves as a diagnostic tool for believers to assess their own spiritual standing by examining these specific moral deficiencies.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Alllah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>saww</sup> inform you of the ones who are the most remote from me<sup>saww</sup> in likeness?’ They said, ‘Yes, O  Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The immoral, the scandalous, the foul-mouthed, the stingy, the rogue, the malicious, the envious, the hard of heart, the one remote from every hope of goodness without any safety from every evil feared’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah once asked, ‘Should I tell you who is more dissimilar to me among you?’ They said, ‘Yes, O Messenger of Allah, please do so.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘He is an indecent, scandalous one, foulmouthed, stingy, deceitful, hateful, envious, and hardhearted who is far from being expected to do any good, and from whom all kinds of frightening evil is expected to emerge.’”
